newsitem.title: CANADA: Northwest Cargo ups ex-Asia contract rates.
newsitem.headline: Northwest Cargo ups ex-Asia contract rates.

text.p: With its ex-Asia cargo volumes firming, Northwest Airlines has begun the process of restoring contract rates to pre-1996 levels, said Northwest Cargo president William Slattery.
Northwest's ex-Asia rates were slashed by as much as 20 percent when the Pacific cargo market slumped last winter and spring, Slattery told Reuters in an interview from Minneapolis.
"Most of the business coming out of Asia is on a contract basis, so we are talking about individual rate increases" negotiated as contracts come due, he added.
"There are some individual contracts that we moved up in July and August and we're moving more up in September and even more in October."
Slattery said his preliminary assessment of the looming October-December peak is that ex-Asia demand will be stronger than last year.

He said his goal is to put ex-Asia rates back to their 1994 peak levels, particularly to bolster the economics of the carrier's eight Boeing 747-200 freighters, all of which operate exclusively on the Pacific.
"Whether we can get there in one year, or it takes a little longer, I'm not sure," he said.
"We were in pretty good financial shape in 1993-94, even 1995, on the freighters.

"But in 1996, rates from Hong Kong and Taipei dropped 20 percent, and did drop - though not as extensively - out of southeast Asia. In the case of Japan, the rates dropped modestly but we got hit year over year by the yen."
To customers who ask about 1997 rates, said Slattery, "I have clearly indicated that we have to get back to a rate structure that's not dissimilar to what we had in 1994."
Slattery said Northwest has had staff discussions in recent days about possible responses to higher jet fuel prices, including levying fuel surcharges. Nothing has been decided, he added.
